rationale: Successor experiment for the growth-sequence investigation, pursuing a concrete unobserved consequence of the recorded finding: after the deposition, can an operator repair the cluster in-process, or does the documented growth mistake leave the cluster unusable until the named server appears. The harness is the same growth staging, extended with two legal repair attempts (removing the absent server, and replacing it with a non-voter) each bounded by a timer, and with a longer three-second window on the unrepaired state, so the observation covers both the API answers and whether any leader emerges. Native local feedback in a scratch copy inside draft showed both calls refused and the node staying a Candidate, but the retained execution decides.

experiment.revision_reason: Same investigation and growth staging, extended after the bounded write attempt with two legal API repair attempts against the dead cluster and a three-second observation of the unrepaired state; the earlier receipt remains the witness for the deposition itself.

scope.description: Two subtests, absent_server and control_present_server, on a one-voter cluster built by MakeCluster(1), calling the public AddVoter for a second server that is either unwired and not running or running beforehand. Each case records the configuration entry's commit status, samples state, term, commit and last index every 25 ms for 1500 ms, makes a bounded client write, then makes two bounded repair attempts on the same node (RemoveServer for the named server and AddNonvoter for it) and finally samples the node every 50 ms for three seconds, before the absent case starts the named server and both cases record whether the cluster recovers.
assumptions: Removing the absent server and replacing it with a non-voter are the two natural in-process attempts to undo the growth step, since a non-voter does not count for quorum.
Each repair attempt is bounded by a timer so that a future which never completes cannot hang the harness.
Bootstrap a single voter and grow it with AddVoter is the sequence BootstrapCluster's documentation recommends.
In-memory LoopbackTransport delivers RPCs in-process without loss, so a refused call reflects the library's own answer.
excluded: No production code is modified and no fault is injected.
No offline recovery (RecoverCluster) and no restart are performed, so the manual recovery route stays unexecuted.

experiment.prefix: The growth subtests print growth_before, growth_window, growth_write_attempt, the new growth_api_repair_attempt (remove_server_error, add_nonvoter_error, unrepaired_state_samples, unrepaired_term_samples, unrepaired_commit_samples over three seconds, and final state, term and commit) and growth_recovery.
